records.r1_evidence: CHEMISTRY/PHYSICS VERDICT: 36.1 is physically plausible but is NOT the better-supported of the two values, and this row carries the weaker provenance of the pair. (1) Phase is physical: gamma-valerolactone (GVL, CAS 108-29-2) melts at -31 C / 244 K and boils at 207-208 C / 480-481 K (PubChem CID 7921 experimental, NTP 1992); at 298.15 K it is a liquid over a 236 K window, so a liquid-phase static permittivity is physically realisable and the phase assignment is sound. (2) Magnitude is physical: GBL (the C4 homologue) has a measured static eps = 41.64 at 298.15 K (ThermoML 10.1021/je900503p, Dekameter, U=0.06 at 95%); GVL has one more CH2 (molar volume 95.4 vs 76.6 cm3/mol) so its number density is 0.80x GBL, and a Kirkwood-Froehlich estimate with the repository's own xTB dipoles (mu_GVL=5.038 D vs mu_GBL=4.936 D, ratio 1.02) gives eps_GVL = 34.9 at g=1.0, spanning 31.5-38.2 for g=0.90-1.10. Both 36.1 and 36.9 fall inside that band, so chemistry cannot discriminate them; the lactone family brackets eps(298 K) at 35-42. (3) The 2.2% spread is NOT inter-laboratory reproducibility: 0.8/36.1 = 2.22%, which exceeds the project's own 2.00% relative tolerance by 1.11x, but the real point is that 2.2% is far SMALLER than the reproducibility actually documented for static permittivity of this exact compound class. The same ThermoML GBL file reports two replicates at 293.15 K (42.34 and 42.81) differing by 0.47 = 1.10%, i.e. 8x its own stated U=0.06, and the literature value commonly quoted for GBL (39.1) differs from the primary 41.64 by 6.1%. A 2.2% gap is therefore within the NOISE of this quantity and is not evidence of a transcription error or a different physical quantity. (4) Both CAN be correct on one eps(T) curve: the measured homologue slope is d(eps)/dT = -0.129 /K (GBL, 293-313 K), so a 0.8 gap corresponds to only 6.2 K (at the local 298-303 K slope of -0.108 /K, 7.4 K). 36.9 at 291.9 K (18.8 C) and 36.1 at 298.15 K lie on the SAME line, and a 25 C vs 20 C labelling difference alone reproduces 81% of the gap. Neither leg reports a temperature: this row's T=298.15 K is flagged temperature_source=review_table_standard_room_temperature, i.e. an ASSUMED standard room temperature, not a reported one, and the 36.9 leg is flagged temperature_source=not_reported. The apparent same-temperature conflict is an artefact of the ingest assigning 298.15 K to two documents that never stated a temperature. (5) Water content: 1.8 wt% H2O would add about +0.8 to eps (linear bound against eps_H2O=78.2), so a small purity difference can also produce the gap in the same direction. DECISION RATIONALE: HOLD rather than PASS because the row has zero contributing observations (ledger search for GAEKPEKOJKCEMS-UHFFFAOYSA-N returns 0 rows), condition_pair_valid=false, NO_BAND_OBSERVATIONS_FOUND, and its 298.15 K is a constructed review-table assumption rather than a reported measurement condition; HOLD rather than FAIL because 36.1 is chemically and physically sound and the review table is a legitimate secondary source. RETAIN_PARALLEL is recommended over choosing a primary because the two values are the same physical quantity within measurement noise, are not independent replications (no primary measurement exists for either), and the 2.2% gap is smaller than the documented spread of the method itself; rejecting either would discard real information and averaging is forbidden by project rule.

records.r1_evidence: CHEMISTRY/PHYSICS VERDICT: 36.9 is marginally the more plausible of the two numbers and is the better-sourced leg, but it is not established as a 298.15 K value and must not be promoted to primary on this evidence. (1) Phase is physical: GVL is a liquid at 298.15 K, mp -31 C (244 K) and bp 207-208 C (480-481 K) per PubChem CID 7921 experimental (NTP 1992); density 1.047-1.054 g/cm3. A liquid-phase static permittivity is realisable with a 236 K liquid window, so the phase assignment is sound. (2) Magnitude: the lactone homology brackets eps(298 K) between GBL (measured 41.64 at 298.15 K, ThermoML 10.1021/je900503p) and the Kirkwood-Froehlich prediction for GVL of 34.9 at g=1.0 (band 31.5-38.2 for g=0.90-1.10 using the repo's xTB dipoles 5.038 D vs 4.936 D and the 0.80x number-density ratio). 36.9 sits near the centre of that band and is the value returned by the live Reaxys index for this substance (probes/reaxys_core_four_crosscheck.csv, location 'supporting information', Segato et al. 2021 Inorg. Chim. Acta 522 120372), and Reaxys holds exactly ONE dielectric row for GVL in the entire substance record. Slight edge to 36.9 over 36.1: the higher value is the one consistent with a normal-purity dry sample read at or slightly below room temperature, and 36.9 is what an independent curated index reproduces, whereas 36.1 exists only as a review-table transcription. (3) The 2.2% gap (0.8/36.1) exceeds the project's 2.00% relative tolerance by 1.11x but is well inside the method's real reproducibility: the primary GBL file carries two replicates at one temperature differing by 1.10% (8x its stated U=0.06), and the commonly quoted GBL value 39.1 differs from the primary 41.64 by 6.1%. So 2.2% is noise, not a transcription error, and not a finite-frequency artefact: the primary GBL comparison was made at zero frequency (ePropName 'Relative permittivity at zero frequency') and both GVL legs are low-frequency/static claims. (4) Both can be simultaneously correct: with d(eps)/dT = -0.129 /K measured on the homologue, the 0.8 gap equals 6.2 K of temperature. 36.9 at 291.9 K (18.8 C) and 36.1 at 298.15 K are the same curve. Critically, this leg reports NO temperature at all (temperature_source=not_reported; the Reaxys row 'has no temperature column at all' per reports/reaxys_core_four_crosscheck.md section 3.3), so its T=298.15 K is an ingest assumption, not a measurement condition, and the 'same temperature' premise of the conflict is unsupported for this leg. Water content is the other legitimate route: about 1.8 wt% H2O raises eps by ~+0.8 (eps_H2O=78.2), so a wetter sample reads high, i.e. toward 36.9, not away from it. (5) The 4th data point argues for caution: the Perricone 2011 thesis Tableau 8 gives 32 at 25 C and elsewhere 34 (reports/g1plus_perricone_thesis_crosscheck.md), which is 11.4% BELOW 36.1 and far outside any rounding or temperature explanation (that would need about 32 K of offset). That widens the true spread of GVL's literature eps to 32-36.9 and shows the field has not converged, so neither of these two rows may be declared the canonical value. DECISION RATIONALE: HOLD because provenance is incomplete (zero contributing observations; ledger search for GAEKPEKOJKCEMS-UHFFFAOYSA-N returns 0 rows), condition_pair_valid=false, NO_BAND_OBSERVATIONS_FOUND, and the 298.15 K is an assumption over a source that explicitly reports no temperature; HOLD rather than FAIL because 36.9 is physically sound, is the only dielectric number the Reaxys index holds for this compound, and comes from a primary-article supporting information rather than a review. RETAIN_PARALLEL over RETAIN_AS_PRIMARY: designating this leg primary would silently assert a temperature the source does not state and would bury the unresolved 32/34 legs; the pair should stand side by side until a temperature-resolved primary measurement is read.
records.r2_evidence: DOI RESOLVES (true). Handle 10.1016/j.ica.2021.120372 -> linkinghub PII S0020169321001286; Crossref: 'Experimental and theoretical investigation of the cycloisomerization of N-propargylcarboxamide catalyzed by NHC-Au-X in green solvents', Inorganica Chimica Acta 522:120372, July 2021, Segato J, Baratta W, Belanzoni P, Belpassi L, Del Zotto A, Zuccaccia D. DOI and citation are real and well formed. THE JOURNAL CHOICE IS DEFENSIBLE BUT GVL'S ROLE IS NOT: Inorg. Chim. Acta is a legitimate venue for gold-NHC catalysis, and the published abstract confirms gamma-valerolactone really is one of the screened solvents ('most of these solvents (cyclohexanone, isopropyl acetate, MIBK, ethyl lactate, furfuryl alcohol, gamma-valerolactone, propylene carbonate and propionic acid) are comparable or better solvents with respect to traditional VOS'). So GVL genuinely appears in this paper - but as a REACTION SOLVENT in a catalysis study, not as a characterised dielectric material. NO EVIDENCE THE PAPER MEASURES PERMITTIVITY: the record points to 'supporting information' as the page; a static epsilon in such an SI table is normally a cited solvent descriptor used to rationalise solvent polarity, not a value these authors measured. The 113 Crossref reference entries contain no dielectric, permittivity, handbook, CRC, Landolt or Wohlfarth item, so the SI table cannot be shown to be a primary measurement; it is at least as likely a compilation. VALUE CANNOT BE VERIFIED: the article is closed access (Unpaywall oa_status='closed', is_oa=false), has no OA copy, and is absent from Europe PMC (hitCount 0 for this DOI). No PDF, SI or page image for this DOI exists anywhere in the repository (searched 115778, 120372, ica.2021, isci, and all PDFs). PROVENANCE CHAIN IS CORRUPT AT ITS ORIGIN: the dielectric_v04.csv notes record that the upstream was a Reaxys queue row carrying NO DOI, and that the queue row mislabelled the compound's InChIKey as JYVATQXCHBTGRN-UHFFFAOYSA-N (not GVL). The DOI was back-resolved through Crossref afterwards; it was never read off a document the project possesses. A post-hoc DOI attribution to an unseen SI is exactly the case where 'DOI resolves' must not be read as 'value is sourced'. TEMPERATURE IS IMPUTED HERE TOO: dielectric_v04.csv temperature_source='not_reported' and gate flag 'temperature_not_reported'; T=298.15 K was imputed by the same room-temperature default as R227. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CONFLICT ITSELF: the premise - same compound, same T=298.15 K, two different epsilon - is not supported. NEITHER leg states 298.15 K. The two rows were placed at a common temperature by an imputation rule, and only then compared. INDEPENDENCE: the pair is not two independent measurements. R227 is a review-table compilation citing a battery paper; R248 is a solvent-properties descriptor in a catalysis SI. Both are almost certainly derived from a shared handbook or compilation lineage, so an independence-based resolution (AVERAGE_JUSTIFIED, or picking one as 'the measurement') would be unsound. LEDGER ABSENCE: same class as R227 - v04row-248 sits in the 33-row ingestion_path='unknown' group of the coverage gap registry, not in the 102-row NBS514_CIRCULAR_MANUAL_ENTRY group, so this is NOT a legitimate manual transcription of a printed handbook. DECISION: FAIL as an evidence row in its current state - not because the DOI is fake (it is real) but because the record asserts an unverified epsilon at an unreported temperature, attributed post hoc to an SI the project has never retrieved, from an upstream row that carried the wrong structure key. evidence_grade=INSUFFICIENT. Do NOT average with R227.

This attack also fails. It is a homogeneous gold-catalysis paper that uses GVL as a reaction medium; the dielectric constant is incidental, appears only in 'supporting information', and its 113 references are all Au-catalysis/green-chemistry work with no dielectric-constant study. The value is therefore a METHODS-TABLE CITATION, not a reported dielectric measurement. The project's 'source_quality=primary' label is an inference from 'this is a research article', not evidence that a permittivity was measured. TEMPERATURE IS ABSENT: temperature_source='not_reported'. The 298.15 K on the row is an IMPUTATION by the queue, not a reported condition - the project's own notes state 'neither leg carries a measurement temperature'. ORIGIN IS NOT INDEPENDENT: the row entered the project through a restricted Reaxys queue row (probes/reaxys_dielectric_queue_first_cut.csv, queue_rank 3) that carried NO DOI and a WRONG InChIKey (JYVATQXCHBTGRN-UHFFFAOYSA-N, which the project itself proved returns 0 substances/0 documents). The DOI was attached afterwards by Crossref lookup. So the provenance chain is: Reaxys record -> unverified DOI attachment -> assumed temperature. ADMISSIBILITY: the best available lead, but a value in an SI table of an unrelated catalysis paper, with no stated temperature, reached through a mis-keyed restricted intermediary. It is not an admissible primary measurement, though it is closer than R227.
